title: GameMaker Library: Timber added, 88 assets
body:
Timber is in the GameMaker Library from today, new here first: it has no page of its own yet. That makes 88 assets on this page. If you own the library, download again from your itch.io library at no extra cost: the whole library holds it in the folder for worlds, skies and places, and NEW 2026-11-16: Timber only holds Timber alone, so you only download what changed.

What Timber is

  • Choppable trees for GameMaker in pure GML, made from the trees already in your game: a sprite you draw, or the trees painted on your tile layer, found as whole trees even when they span several tiles.
  • Each blow shudders the tree and opens a notch in its own bark while chips and leaves fly. The last blow brings it down in one of 8 ways: topple, crash, snap, whip, uproot, slice, shatter or burn, always away from the striker.
  • The crown breaks into clumps and leaves cut from its own pixels, the trunk splits into logs cut from its own bark, a stump with a ringed cut face stays, and after a while it grows back from a sapling. A tile tree goes back on your layer as the exact tiles you painted.
  • 6 kinds of tree (broadleaf, conifer, palm, dead, birch, giant mushroom) by 8 falls makes 48 styles, every number a slider. A runnable demo room, THE WOODLOT, with a woodcutter and a browser of all 48.
  • Reading a tree out of its sprite takes about 4 ms once, when you create it, in the VM build on the test machine.

It is the first of three Timber, Tide and Fathom systems for outdoor worlds: water surfaces and underwater levels come next. Timber is a GameMaker port of our Timber for RPG Maker MZ and for Godot 4.

The library now holds 88 assets worth $1,105.12 bought one by one, for $19.99; 11 of them are worlds, skies and places. Every new asset joins on its launch day. The price rises as the library grows: $5 more for new buyers each time three more assets join, $24.99 at 89 assets and $29.99 at 92, never more, and every step will be announced here first with its date. If you own it, you never pay again. Try the free sampler, Drawn in Code, and if the library helps your game, a quick rating is the best way to support it.

Made with AI tools: the code and the store images.
